adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — updateEvent's fallback `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it is always undefined and legacy references without externalCalendarId now update `calendarId: undefined` instead of the destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it then does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since `externalCalendarId` is falsy in that branch, the `find` predicate will almost never match and `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` rather than falling back to a destination calendar (previously `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This is a real logic error introduced by the diff and can route updates to an undefined/incorrect calendar (or default behavior elsewhere) for legacy cases without `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — deleteEvent has the same always-undefined `find`, so cancels for references without externalCalendarId now hit `"primary"`, and the 404 handler resolves successfully, leaving an orphaned external event while cal.com reports the booking cancelled.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the updated `deleteEvent` calendarId selection is:
```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
When `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null` (the exact case mentioned), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined`), which will almost always return no match, making `calendarId` undefined and causing the call to fall back to the default (`"primary"`). This is a real behavioral bug introduced by the refactor from a single `destinationCalendar` object to an array, because it no longer correctly picks a destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:76 — Office365 (and lark/CalDAV) still use destinationCalendar[0].externalId unencoded in the Graph path for every host credential, so a collective booking attempts to write host A's calendar id using host B's token

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` now iterates over each destination calendar/credential (packages/core/EventManager.ts, loop over `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`). However Office365 (and Lark, and the CalDAV base service) still derive the target calendar ID from only the *first* destination calendar: Office365 uses `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` then builds `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), and Lark/CalDAV similarly take `[0]`. Since the provider `createEvent` calls for non-Google calendars do not use the per-destination `externalId` passed into `createEvent()` (it’s only returned in the `EventResult`), a collective booking with multiple destination calendars can attempt to insert into destinationCalendar[0] using another host’s credential/token.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:759 — New loadUsers catch re-throws Prisma error messages verbatim as a 400 to unauthenticated bookers, leaking model/field and query details

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` was changed to wrap its logic in a `try/catch` and, on `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError`, it throws `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`. This directly propagates Prisma’s raw `error.message` to the HTTP response (400), which can reveal internal schema/query details (model/field names, constraint info, etc.) to the requester. The diff shows this new behavior explicitly in the catch block; previously there was no such re-throw of Prisma messages as client-visible 400 errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:423 — No test for cancelling a recurring collective booking with multiple calendar references: the recurring-delete branch now runs once per reference, issuing duplicate deleteEvent calls per booking

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the code changed from a single calendar reference (`find`) to multiple (`filter`) and now iterates `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. In the recurring-delete branch (inside `if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings)`), the deletion logic ignores the current `reference` and instead loops over *all* `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(..._calendar)` and *all* `updatedBookings`, pushing `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` for each. Because this whole recurring-delete block now runs once per reference, it will repeat the same delete operations multiple times when there are multiple calendar references, causing duplicate `deleteEvent` calls.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:358 — Partial-failure path untested: a 404 from one host's calendar makes createEvent resolve with success:false and no createdEvent, yet createAllCalendarEvents still pushes it, so the booking is reported created with a missing calendar entry

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `createEvent` in `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` catches a 404 and returns `undefined` from the integration call, but still returns an `EventResult` object with `success = false` and `createdEvent` unset. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, the code does `const createdEvent = await createEvent(...); if (createdEvent) createdEvents.push(createdEvent);`—since `createdEvent` here is the `EventResult` object (truthy even on failure), failure results will be pushed. Whether this causes the booking to be "reported created with a missing calendar entry" depends on downstream handling (not shown in the diff), so the finding’s described end-user impact isn’t fully verifiable from the diff alone, but the partial-failure path/handling concern is diff-grounded.
